title: AiDocument
description: A visual answer for the user, rendered top to bottom as an ordered list of blocks. Mix text and charts freely, e.g. heading → stats → bar_chart → heading → paragraph → pie_chart. Guidelines: open with the answer (a lead paragraph or stats), then evidence. Give every chart a nearby sentence saying what to notice; don't repeat the chart's numbers in prose. Use a row to show 2–3 related charts side by side (they stack on phones). Prefer one well-chosen chart over several similar ones.

oneOf.description: A section heading. Use level 1 for each major section of the answer, 2 for sub-sections. Sentence case, no trailing period. Keep it short; a heading that states the takeaway ("Dining is up 18%") beats a label ("Dining").

Body text. Supports inline Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [label](https://url). Separate paragraphs with a blank line. Put the key number in **bold**. Keep paragraphs short (1–3 sentences) and place them next to the chart they explain.
A bulleted or numbered list. Use for 2–7 parallel points or steps. Inline Markdown allowed in items.

A highlighted box for one important message. info = neutral tip or context; success = goal reached, good news; warning = something to watch (approaching a limit); danger = a real problem (over budget, missed payment). Use at most one or two per response.
1–4 headline numbers shown as tiles (e.g. total spent, saved, net worth). Use instead of a chart when the answer is a single number or a few. Put it near the top of a response.
A thin horizontal rule between unrelated parts. Rarely needed: headings already separate sections.

Render a bar chart. Use for comparing amounts across categories (spending by category, income vs spending by month). Not for trends over many time points (use a line chart) or a single headline number.
Render a line chart. Use for trends over time or any ordered x (balances, net worth, projections). Use a bar chart to compare separate categories.
Render a histogram: how values of ONE measure are distributed (e.g. transaction sizes). Send raw values and let the chart bin them, or send bins.

Render a donut/pie showing how ONE whole splits into a few parts, read at a glance. Max 4 coloured slices; the rest fold into grey "Other". Do NOT use to compare close values, rank many parts, or show change over time — use a bar chart. Avoid 2-slice pies.
Render a scatter plot: the relationship between two measures (e.g. income vs savings rate per month). Up to 3 coloured groups.
Render a Gantt chart: tasks, phases or goals on a calendar, with progress, milestones and dependencies.

rowBlock.description: Place 2–3 blocks side by side (usually charts or stats). Stacks vertically on small screens. Rows can't be nested.

columns.description: Defaults to the number of blocks (max 3).

heading.title: HeadingSpec
heading.description: A section heading. Use level 1 for each major section of the answer, 2 for sub-sections. Sentence case, no trailing period. Keep it short; a heading that states the takeaway ("Dining is up 18%") beats a label ("Dining").

text.description: Heading text. Inline **bold**/*italic* allowed but rarely needed.

paragraph.title: ParagraphSpec
paragraph.description: Body text. Supports inline Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [label](https://url). Separate paragraphs with a blank line. Put the key number in **bold**. Keep paragraphs short (1–3 sentences) and place them next to the chart they explain.

size.description: lead = larger intro/summary sentence at the top; small = footnotes, caveats, sources.

list.title: ListSpec
list.description: A bulleted or numbered list. Use for 2–7 parallel points or steps. Inline Markdown allowed in items.

ordered.description: true for numbered steps where order matters.

callout.title: CalloutSpec
callout.description: A highlighted box for one important message. info = neutral tip or context; success = goal reached, good news; warning = something to watch (approaching a limit); danger = a real problem (over budget, missed payment). Use at most one or two per response.

title.description: Short bold first line. Defaults to Note / Good news / Heads up / Warning.

stats.title: StatsSpec
stats.description: 1–4 headline numbers shown as tiles (e.g. total spent, saved, net worth). Use instead of a chart when the answer is a single number or a few. Put it near the top of a response.

label.description: What the number is, e.g. "Spent in October".

value.description: A raw number (formatted with `format`) or a pre-formatted string.

change.description: Change vs. the comparison period. A number is a percent (12 → "+12%") unless changeFormat says otherwise; a string is shown as-is ("+$240").

goodDirection.description: Which direction is good. Spending: down. Savings: up. none = always neutral colour.

divider.title: DividerSpec
divider.description: A thin horizontal rule between unrelated parts. Rarely needed: headings already separate sections.

bar_chart.title: BarChartSpec
bar_chart.description: Render a bar chart. Use for comparing amounts across categories (spending by category, income vs spending by month). Not for trends over many time points (use a line chart) or a single headline number.

title.description: Short chart title, sentence case. Say what is measured, e.g. "Spending by category, October".

subtitle.description: Optional context line: units, period, or the takeaway.

categories.description: Labels along the category axis, in display order. Keep them short.

series.description: One entry per measure. Up to 4 are coloured; a 5th is grey; more are folded into "Other". Keep the same order across charts so colours stay consistent.

values.description: One number per category, same order as `categories`. null = no data.

color.description: Optional. Pin a colour so the same entity matches across charts. Omit to use palette order.

orientation.description: vertical = columns (good for time periods). horizontal = bars (good for long category names or many categories).

layout.description: grouped compares series side by side; stacked shows parts summing to a total; percent shows each category's composition as 100%.

style.description: percent means values are already percentages (45 = 45%).

min.description: Must be ≤ 0; bars always start at zero.

valueLabels.description: Which bars print their value. Be selective; tooltips and the table already show every value. totals applies to stacked layouts.

highlight.description: Category names to emphasise (others are dimmed). Use to point at what your answer is about.

referenceLines.description: Rules at a value, e.g. a budget or savings target.

sort.description: Sort categories by total. Don't sort time periods.

height.description: Vertical charts only; horizontal charts size to their rows.

line_chart.title: LineChartSpec
line_chart.description: Render a line chart. Use for trends over time or any ordered x (balances, net worth, projections). Use a bar chart to compare separate categories.

title.description: Short title, sentence case. Say what is measured.

subtitle.description: Optional context: units, period, or the takeaway.

x.description: X values in order: ISO dates ("2026-03-01" or "2026-03"), numbers, or short category labels.

xType.description: Optional; detected from x when omitted.

series.description: One entry per line. ≤4 stay distinguishable; more are drawn grey.

values.description: One per x. null leaves a gap.

color.description: Optional. Pin so the same entity matches across charts.

curve.description: step for values that change in jumps (balances after deposits).

area.description: Light wash under the line. Best with one series.

valueLabels.description: Which points print their value. Be selective.

endLabels.description: Series names at line ends. Default on for 2–4 series when they don't collide.

highlight.description: Series names to emphasise; others turn grey.

forecastFrom.description: The x value where actuals end and projection begins; the rest is dashed and labelled Projected.

style.description: percent means values are already percentages (45 = 45%).

includeZero.description: Set false to zoom into a narrow range (e.g. 98–104).

referenceLines.description: Horizontal rules, e.g. a savings goal.

histogram.title: HistogramSpec
histogram.description: Render a histogram: how values of ONE measure are distributed (e.g. transaction sizes). Send raw values and let the chart bin them, or send bins.

title.description: Short title, sentence case. Say what is measured.

subtitle.description: Optional context: units, period, or the takeaway.

values.description: Raw observations. Preferred: enables mean/median markers.

bins.description: Pre-binned data, used instead of values.

binCount.description: Approximate bin count; widths are rounded to clean numbers.

style.description: percent means values are already percentages (45 = 45%).

referenceLines.description: Vertical rules on the value axis.

pie_chart.title: PieChartSpec
pie_chart.description: Render a donut/pie showing how ONE whole splits into a few parts, read at a glance. Max 4 coloured slices; the rest fold into grey "Other". Do NOT use to compare close values, rank many parts, or show change over time — use a bar chart. Avoid 2-slice pies.

title.description: Short title, sentence case. Say what is measured.

subtitle.description: Optional context: units, period, or the takeaway.

donut.description: Ring with the total in the centre.

style.description: percent means values are already percentages (45 = 45%).

minSharePercent.description: Slices below this share fold into Other.

scatter_plot.title: ScatterPlotSpec
scatter_plot.description: Render a scatter plot: the relationship between two measures (e.g. income vs savings rate per month). Up to 3 coloured groups.

title.description: Short title, sentence case. Say what is measured.

subtitle.description: Optional context: units, period, or the takeaway.

size.description: Optional third measure drawn as dot area.

series.description: Grouped points. More than 3 groups fold into grey Other.

size.description: Optional third measure drawn as dot area.

style.description: percent means values are already percentages (45 = 45%).
percent means values are already percentages (45 = 45%).

gantt_chart.title: GanttChartSpec
gantt_chart.description: Render a Gantt chart: tasks, phases or goals on a calendar, with progress, milestones and dependencies.

title.description: Short title, sentence case. Say what is measured.

subtitle.description: Optional context: units, period, or the takeaway.

id.description: Referenced by dependsOn. Defaults to name.

end.description: ISO date. Or use durationDays. Omit both for a milestone.

group.description: Tasks in a group share a colour (≤4 groups coloured).

dependsOn.description: ids or names of tasks that must finish first.

today.description: Today rule: true/false or an ISO date. Default: shown when in range.
